newsitem.title: USA: US March T-bond end up after impressive late rally.
newsitem.headline: US March T-bond end up after impressive late rally.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures closed higher, with March T-bonds staging an impressive rally after the last leg of the U.S. Treasury's quarterly refunding auction ended better than anticipated, traders said.
"There were some expectations that the 30-year bond auction would be as disappointing as the 10-year note auction," one bond futures trader said.

Most traders and analysts said the actual results of the $10 billion 30-year bond auction were neutral, and that the market also rallied due to relief that the U.S. Treasury department's $39.75 billion quarterly refunding had ended.
"The market seems relieved that the auctions are out of the way more than anything else," one futures trader said.
In addition, some analysts said buying from portfolio managers and hedge funds was heavy due to underlying concerns about an absence of supply.
Mortgage-backed dealers also emerged as good buyers, as 30-year bond yields dropped towards 6.60/61 percent after the results of the bond auction were released, they said.
Traders estimated bond futures volume at about 500,000 contracts, and said longs were probably added to the already lofty open interest levels.
Open interest for all bond futures traded at the CBOT set a record high of 542,330 on Wednesday, up 11,535 from Tuesday, according to the CBOT's final figures.
Record open interest led some traders to expect a "head-fake" in which prices could initially sway one way before following their long-term trend in the other direction.

"I'm wondering if what we are seeing is a head-fake," one bond futures trader said when March bonds initially stalled at 113-01/32. "We could be 'painting the tape,' or just adding weak longs before selling this market down."
However, March knocked through 113-09/32 within minutes.

March's ability to hold above the one-month high of 113-00 and grind up to 113-12/32 within the closing minutes of pit trade convinced several sources that the contract is poised to test 113-26/32 on Friday. A rise to 113-26/32 would mean March has retraced 62 percent of its two-month downmove.
March bonds initially dipped slightly after the auction results showed an average yield of 6.64 percent, above estimates for a yield of 6.63 percent.
"Locals got short the way they do ahead of every auction, but just found bids all the way underneath," one trader said.
Traders said activity could be volatile on Friday after the U.S. January Producer Price Index is released.

Traders and dealers will only have until midday to square positions ahead of a long U.S. holiday weekend. On Friday CME Eurodollar futures close at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and CBOT bond futures end at 1210 CST/1810 GMT, ahead of the U.S. Presidents' Day holiday on Monday.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were up 30/32 at 113-11/32, 10-year notes were up 15/32 at 109-30/32, June Eurodollars were up three bps at 94.38, and September Eurodollars rose seven bps at 94.28.
